memos.Sleepover notes:
He is a lovely boy, and I'm very impressed with him and wanted to share as Madison mentioned fosters should share notes to help find him his forever home so here's what I've got so far along with some pictures.

Collie/Pitbull Mix
He is off to a great start but doesn't seem fully housebroken yet: we had a couple misses at the door and perhaps one marking in the house. Generally, he goes outside but you have to tell him he has to use the potty and take frequent visits especially after drinking water or eating and waking up from naps, he does not signal that HE knows he needs the potty yet.
Very snuggly velcro dog! (typical pitbull) Was my shadow in under 3 hours of handling him. Thinks he's a lap dog. Gets very anxious if you leave the room without him and follows you immediately.
A little nipping (not just mouthing on my hands but nipping on my pants and clothes like a collie), but takes correction to chew toys pretty well, you must repeat but he eventually takes the hint.
Update as of this morning Mon Jul 20, he is nipping excessively and had blown through 2 forever chews/has begun destructive chewing on furniture. Will get more chews but it seems once he gets familiar with the house he is prone to chewing on everything.
This was as of Sunday afternoon - Impressively he has only attempted nibbling on my wicker basket so far. Generally not nibbling on my furniture and redirects to his forever chews pretty well.
Very playful with the toys, has bursts of energy but not an endurance athlete as of yet.
He points/fixates on lizards and birds on walks or in the backyard. He does startle at the TV or gets worked up when you show him Dog TV with birds and squirrels.
I was told he is dog friendly, however I did not test this as he got his little puppy self very worked barking very loud up every time a dog passed by within about 10-12 feet at a dog friendly patio on leash today, he did calm down once the dogs stayed put a good 15-20 feet and was very relaxed but alerted quickly whenever one came near. We took several calm down breaks further away and came back to the people when he relaxed.
UPDATE: Very reactive to dogs 20+ft away, if in sight he whines and barks very loud pulling at the leash and lunging towards the direction of the dogs. He does calm down, and he got better about ignoring dogs behind fences when we tried to run a bit this morning.
Walks - pulls like a typical new pup, once tired out/about 40min of walking he stays to the side of you as coached and is less reactive to passing dogs and bugs/lizards.
Crates himself! - he seems very amenable to two crates I have for him, I'm not sure if he actually understands the command crate but he has comfortably been in both so far, one zipped up for the night in my room with me.
UPDATE: We protested staying in our crate last night. He stays in it well if you're nearby but he'd rather be in your bed or constantly played with or petted.
Keeps jumping on the couch, but we are slowly learning not to do that, especially if we need to 'dig', and we are understanding 'off' slowly.
Loves his kibble, not very patient about waiting for his bowl to be ready once he smells the kibble/hears the bag but we're working on that.
Slowly getting 'sit', starting to learn 'forward' on walks.
Very picky about snacks, didn't seem to like the bag of doggy treats I selected for him.
Pretty good about not begging.
Adorable, sleepy boy, at home and in the car. Very well behaved passenger.
Does NOT like to be left outside alone (closed my glass sliding door to see what he'd do, turns out, sit wait by the door and be a bit sassy when he was let in)
Seems to inherently understand 'fetch' already
LOVES new people, practically melted for my neighbors and rolled over for belly rubs
It is hot out, but given his very short coat and lean frame he still seems a little more sensitive to overheating than I'd expect - throughout today, even relaxed on the patio next to a fan he drank a lot of water and got very hot, he fell asleep as soon as he was in air conditioning. This behavior was the same after our early morning walk today. He took about 3 water breaks/rest in the shade to make it through (about a 2mile walk very good for a pup his age actually)
Seems to have allergies and dry skin (very pitbull like) I washed him off at home in the tub yesterday to get the shelter poo and dirt off him, he did a GREAT job at letting me bathe him although he was a little scared. I notice the bumps I'm seeing are just lumps of dried skin. I'm not sure how to help him with that but if you have a suggestion please let me know.
Not clear on his vocal tendencies - first day he was totally silent. Today we barked at the delivery, the dogs on the walk and at me for not putting the food bowl down fast enough.

Given how velcro and variable his energy is, I'm concerned I'm a fair, but not ideal, home for him as I am a hybrid employee and am commuting from cedar park to downtown/away 3 days a week for 4-7hours each time. I also typically go for very long runs (5-8mile walk/runs about a 2.5 hour trips, home to track to back home), I don't know if that will ever be his thing since he's little, shows promise. I have yet to see how he fairs in his crate alone for a few hours. Seems more prone to have bursts of energy throughout the day and very much is an 'indoor dog'

He is VERY lovable though. I think he will make a great addition to a family with kiddos who intermittently want to play fetch with the dog or someone who is fully remote. He needs constant focus and nearby presence.

animals.kennelCardMemo:
Cuddly, Affectionate, Chatty


Looking for a best friend who believes every day should include cuddles, conversation, and just the right number of treats? Tide is ready to fill the position!

This beautiful girl has a calm, gentle spirit and a heart full of love. While she's a little reserved when meeting new people, it doesn't take long before she's rubbing her soft little head against your hand, asking for pets and reminding you that affection is one of life's greatest joys.

Tide is the perfect companion for anyone who enjoys peaceful days at home. She's not one for wild adventures or marathon zoomie sessions. Instead, she's happiest relaxing nearby, soaking up gentle pets, leaning into a good brushing, or curling up for a cozy cuddle. She's wonderfully affectionate while still respecting your space, often doing her own thing before wandering over to collect another round of love.

One thing you'll notice right away is that Tide has plenty to say! She loves chatting with her people, whether she's following you with cheerful commentary after you leave the room or delivering an enthusiastic speech about why she absolutely deserves another treat. Her adorable meows are all part of her irresistible purrsonality!

Tide appreciates having a quiet hideaway when something startles her. A cozy bed, a covered cat cave, or another peaceful retreat helps her feel safe until she's ready to rejoin the action. Tide also has one delightfully quirky preference: she's a fan of running water! If there's a fountain bubbling away, you'll likely have one very happy kitty.

Tide has not been acquainted with other cats or dogs, so any future introductions should be done slowly and thoughtfully. She has, however, been friendly with teenagers and enjoys being around kind people who are happy to share plenty of affection.


If you're searching for a tender, adorable, soft, and talkative companion who will fill your home with gentle head bumps, loving cuddles, and charming conversations, Tide is ready to make a splash in your heart! Contact us about her today!


All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Tide, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org

animals.name: Katie Katwalk
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Gorgeous, Loving, People-oriented

Katie Katwalk is ready to walk her way right into your heart! This sweet girl always wants to be right where you are and loves connecting with her people. Whether that’s simply hanging out in the same room as you or reaching out with a gentle paw to touch your face, Katie Katwalk wants you to know she’s happy to be near you.

Katie Katwalk came to Austin Pets Alive! from Uvalde following the floods, and she’s shown what a resilient and loving kitty she truly is. She still has lots of kitten energy and gets the zoomies often, and you’ll catch her playing with the most random items she can find! But once playtime is over, Katie Katwalk is ready for cuddles, rubbing against your legs and making endless biscuits. She has a soft voice and only meows on occasion.

In her foster home, Katie Katwalk has shown a gentle, easygoing nature around other cats. While she can be a little shy at first, she warms up at her own pace and enjoys lounging on the bed alongside her feline foster friends. Because of her more reserved nature, she would do best in a quieter home without rowdy dogs or kids. Otherwise, her affectionate, snuggly demeanor makes her a wonderful fit for almost any family looking for the sweetest kitty friend!

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Katie Katwalk, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

Finding a devoted companion who seamlessly balances an active spirit with a gentle heart is a wonderful discovery. Big Tan Boy is a sweet-natured fellow who approaches his human friends with an endearing, close-up charm. He has a unique way of sharing affection by gently leaning up to give cozy hugs, resting right in your arms for a sweet moment of connection. He thrives on this personal time, maintaining an upbeat, friendly focus that makes spending time together feel incredibly rewarding.

His playful nature extends to his canine peers as well, and he brings a highly social energy to shelter dog playgroups where he actively romps and has fun with other dogs. Once the energy of the day winds down, he is just as eager to transition into a companionable cuddling partner. If you are looking for a lively, loving friend to share both active trails and relaxing moments, he is ready to jump into your life. Meet Big Tan Boy and bring him home today.

animals.name: Dodger
animals.kennelCardMemo:
With a moniker like Dodger, one might expect a canine who avoids attention or slips away when people approach. However, this good-natured companion proves to be exactly the opposite of her name. Instead of evading connection, she acts as an ultimate embracer, greeting people with a charming and sweet disposition that immediately draws you in. Her affectionate personality shines when she leans in closely to look for cuddles and gentle kisses during her time spent out and about.

This companionable explorer balances her independent nature with an enduring appreciation for people time. When navigating the outdoors, she can be found happily sniffing through the grass and exploring her surroundings at her own pace. Once her curiosity is satisfied, she regularly returns right to your side to seek out a comfortable spot for sun-bathing or to engage in a lighthearted game of chase. While she occasionally shows her playful side with a bit of jumpy excitement, she consistently tries to keep her interactions gentle and nurturing.

Finding her favorite spots is part of her endearing charm, especially when it comes to standard hands-on affection. If you happen to scratch her in just the right place along her neck, she treats you to a classic scratch reflex, happily thumping her back leg in absolute satisfaction. Her sociable behavior also extends to other dogs, as she regularly participates in group play sessions with her fellow canine peers. This approachable girl is ready to bring her calm, sweet energy into a brand new routine. Reach out today to schedule a visit and experience her wonderful hugs for yourself.

animals.name: Snowball (Mochi)
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Mellow, Loving, Chill

Say hello to Snowball! This elegant lady is so ready to snuggle up in her forever lap! She is very sweet and easygoing with a true passion for lounging.

Snowball is one of our intake kitties from the 2026 Central Texas floods. We’re so glad this precious girl is safe and staying warm, dry and cozy with us. She absolutely adores plushies and has the cutest way of curling up with them to nap or making biscuits on them. When she is in the mood for playtime, which doesn’t happen all that often, give her some balls and she will have a blast!

Snowball is not very vocal. But, if you talk to her she is glad to respond! Her luscious ivory coat is so soft to the touch, she has stunning blue eyes and, did you notice she has extra toes? Yes, she’s polydactyl!

Snowball would be so happy in a home with welcoming laps, soft pillows and cushy plushies! She is so exceptionally beautiful inside and out and... those toes! Ernest Hemingway would surely want to keep her and you will too! Contact us for an introduction!

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Snowball, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org

animals.name: Taco Night
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Calm, Cuddly, Curious

Taco Night likes to crank the affection to max capacity! She loves to be pet, including on her belly. Once she feels safe with you, she will gladly snuggle up for love and attention. When she is not cuddling with you, Taco Night can be found lounging around somewhere or in a cool, dark space where she can hide out. When she emerges from a hiding spot, Taco Night will give a BIGGGG stretch.

Taco Night chirps now and then to say hi, but does not talk much otherwise. She is known for having a super-duper loud purr! Taco Night will purr forever when you pet her.

Taco Night would like a home where she can explore, cuddle, and lounge. She loves a hidey-hole and would likely prefer a lower-energy household. Taco Night has also done well around the resident cat in her foster home; she has been described as neutral and curious.

To quote her foster: “I'd adopt her if I could. You should. Please. Seriously. She's a 10/10 cat.” If that does not convince you to give this sweet girl a chance, I do not know what will.

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Taco Night, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

memos.Foster Notes:
He is SUCH a sweet dog that wants nothing more than pets, love and attention. He is a rambunctious puppy full of energy. He loves exploring and can play all day. Bear has been getting used to walking on a leash and is a very quick learner. Over the past two weeks he has learned "sit," "lay down," "touch," and "up." He wants to be by your side all day and will follow you anywhere.

Bear loves other animals. With him being such a big and energetic puppy its best for him to have other big dogs that are tolerant of rowdy play. He also is extremely interested in housecats, all he wants is to be friends but since he's still learning to respect their space, a house with a cat might not be the best fit without additional training.

Bear needs plenty of toys and things to keep him occupied. He explores the world with his mouth, picking up anything and everything he can get his hands (mouth) on, but he is VERY good at listening to "Drop it". He often goes from toy to toy in the house, and especially loves squeak toys, ropes and anything interactive like the "flirt" (basically a fluffy squeak toy on a fishing rod).

Bear is a genuine loving dog, he is so sweet that it's very easy to forgive and forget any of the downsides of having a gigantic energetic puppy. Bear will make an awesome addition to any kind home, as long as you have time and patience for him.
memos.Behavior Team FFU:
from the sleepover host: We would like to extend our overnight stay for another week. We're not sure if we will be able to foster long term as we're still in the process of introducing him to our other animals. He is a bit higher energy than we expected which is causing some tension. We're working on how to get some of that energy out. When we took him home we discussed getting him fixed as soon as possible and we're hoping that can curb some of his craziness. Please let us know when that can be scheduled.

There are several things we've discovered:
We've only had 3 pee accidents in the house and no poop accidents. Two were on the first day we had him so we think it's just that he wasn't sure how to ask to be let out
He is not aggressive at all: no resource guarding, no aggression towards our other pets, we're able to touch his face, paws, etc. with no concerns. If he oversteps with one of our dogs and gets a corrective growl, he will flop over and show his belly. Very submissive
He hardly barks
He is not crate trained but we are working on it. He is fine when he is in the crate (no barking or whining or trying to get out) but we have to physically put him in the crate
He is incredibly smart. We've already been able to teach him "sit", "lay down", and "touch" (putting his nose to our palm). He's almost mastered "up" as well. We're still working on "paw" and "in a circle."
He only likes chicken flavoured treats
The only time he tries to get onto furniture is if someone is on it and wants to get on their lap
His favorite toys are squeaky toys and the flirt. He is not interested in tug of war at all and is only mildly into fetch but only the throw part and not the giving back part
He is a very very sweet boy

Now for the bad news:
Paul has not been properly socialized with other dogs. While he is eager to please and wants to play, he gets in other dogs' faces which upsets them
He is not leash trained and lunges at other dogs (he wants to play with, not harm them but sounds aggressive). We are working on it but we can't get his energy out with long walks because they are slow going with the training. It's also a million degrees out so we only have limited windows to try
He has puppy problems
He's destroyed a pillow, a dog bed, and chewed up part of the carpet (he only does these bad things when I'm on meetings and can't catch him in the act 😭)
He's constantly getting in our other pets faces to the point where our gentle "loves all creatures and wants to be friends with them" dog doesn't want to interact with him
Jumping and nipping are big problems. Because he's so big, the nipping legitimately hurts. We're doing our best to discourage the behaviours but these are our biggest problems
We know that those issues are typical for puppies but him being 70lbs means that the impact of those behaviors is greater. We also know that giving him an outlet for that energy will help so we're trying to figure out how best to do that. Learning tricks helps and we have high hopes for the flirt which we've just introduced. Again, we think that getting him fixed will help so please let us know how soon that can be scheduled.
sent resources addressing issues.

Meet Juan Garcia, a happy, resilient boy who is ready to find his forever home! Found during a flood rescue, Juan has put his past behind him. His embedded collar wound has completely healed, and he greets every single day with pure joy.

Juan makes everyday living a breeze. He is already house trained, crate trained, and eager to make friends with every person he meets on his adventures.

Whether you are looking for an affectionate couch companion, a fun play partner, or a loyal best friend who will always be thrilled to see you, Juan Garcia is ready to fill your home with love. Connect with us today to meet this sweet, resilient boy!

animals.name: Little Dude
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Hi, I'm Little Dude! I'm a year-old Golden Retriever/Lab mix, and I've been spending time in a foster home! My foster family says I am an amazing, perfect-sized boy, and they shared these great notes about me:

I love other dogs and would do fantastic in a home with a playful canine sibling or siblings who love to play. I love zipping around outside with my toys and playing fetch. But once outdoor play is over, I calm down nicely and am completely relaxed while inside.

Beyond dogs, I am a total farm-pro! I am used to cats, horses, and donkeys, and I've even been introduced to chickens. I also do great with kids, though I might jump up occasionally when I get super excited to see them.

I am crate trained at night and while my humans are away, and I have wonderful indoor manners. Having a doggie door and a yard is my absolute dream.

I'm looking for a fun, loving family who will toss the ball with me, give me a yard to run in, and maybe supply a playful canine brother or sister. Think that could be you?

Adoption fee includes spay/neuter, vaccinations, microchip, and lifetime behavior support from Austin Pets Alive!

animals.name: Columbo
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Falling asleep in your arms with a purr is Columbo, a loving, adorable kitty who is always down for a good cuddle session! This sweet girl is incredibly friendly, and loves to let her human friends pick her up and even give her belly rubs/ chin scratches whenever they get the chance!

Although she may be small, don’t let Columbo’s size fool you: this girl loves to give her foster brother, Max, a run for his money when it’s wrestling time, as she is not one to back down on a challenge! As much as she enjoys playtime, Columbo also loves to plot down on the floor and chill out for a nice nap: a girl with good taste, you must admit!

Columbo grew up with her brother, Max, and the two are deeply connected to one another. Oftentimes, these kitties can be found cuddling for comfort, eating together, or simply chasing each other’s tails throughout the halls, as they truly share a unique bond with one another. Ideally, Columbo would love to come home with her brother. Learn more about Max at the link below, and thank you for considering keeping these two lovebugs together! https://tinyurl.com/mr2ym3r2

When it comes to her ideal home, Columbo would thrive in an environment with human friends who are looking for a kitty who loves to give and receive lots and lots of love! animals.kennelCardMemo:
Don't let the name fool you—Prank Caller is no trick, just a pure treat of a companion. This big guy sports a thick, fluffy fawn coat paired with a prominent black mask that frames his soulful dark eyes. His most endearing trait might be his ears, with one standing perfectly tall while the other folds forward in a permanent look of curiosity. While the busy shelter environment can make him feel a bit shy and reserved at first, his friendly nature shines through once he realizes he is safe in your company.

He arrived during the 2026 floods, proving himself to be a resilient survivor who handles life's storms with quiet grace. Prank Caller is neutered, gets along well with other dogs, and prefers gentle, steady interactions over loud, chaotic spaces. He is ready to trade the noisy kennel lifestyle for a calm home where his genuine, loyal personality can truly unfold. Bring Prank Caller into your life today to secure a faithful, steady friend for the long haul.

animals.name: Ozzie
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Hi! I'm Ozzie, your future bundle of joy! I'm all about fun and games, always ready for an adventure or a good play session. I'm smart and quick to learn, so we can master new tricks together. I walk nicely on a leash (bikes, cars, barking dogs, little kids on scooters, and strangers don’t phase me), making every stroll enjoyable. After a day of excitement, I'm happy to relax in my crate, dreaming of our next day together.

I’m a social butterfly and love everyone, bringing smiles and energy wherever I go. I love being active and can get pretty hyped up when excited, but I respond well to gentle corrections because I want to please my people. I'm still learning my name, but I do come when called. I would thrive in a household where both my mind and body are kept active.

If you're looking for a loyal friend with a silly side to share in all your adventures and cozy nights, I'm your guy. Let's make every moment count together!

memos.Volunteer Notes:
How long was your Sleepover
One week, but would love to extend :) Wanted to add stuff to this form now though!

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Velcro Dog
Social Butterfly
Active
Adventurous
Cheerful
Eager-to-please
Fun-loving
Obedient
Silly
Smart

What made you smile or laugh about them?
The way he goes absolutely ballistic when he gets excited

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
Ozzie is an incredibly loving, curious, active, attuned dog. Like any heeler, he needs a lot of stimulation, but he is much calmer than any other heeler I've met. He doesn't seem to be reactive hardly at all, and always seems to check in before doing anything. He's headstrong but in such a respectful way. He gets pretty jumpy when he's hyped, but he responds well to gentle correction and wants to obey! With some training he will be an incredible companion. Already a great walker, and is unbothered by: bikes, cars, other dogs (nice), other dogs (barking at us), little kids on scooters, strangers, and a small unleashed dog who ran right up to him to say hi. He pulls a lot but once he's tired he drops right in next to me, and will definitely respond well to structured walk training. He doesn't know his name yet but comes when called! He's a picky potty-er but didn't have any accidents inside! It might take awhile for him to go (at least for now).

Where did the dog sleep
Crate

How was the dog in the car?
Anxious and restless
Some whining or pacing, but settled

How was the dog when left alone?
Relaxed

What is their housetraining status?
Fully housetrained - Consistently holds it when left alone, and gives clear signals when they need to go outside. May have had accidents in the first couple days, but leveled out completely once the dog learned the routines.

How did the dog do in the bath?
Did not attempt to give the dog a bath

How did they do with other adults in the home or visitors? Did they meet visitors, or only hang with you?
Loved everyone

How did they do with cats or small animals (if present)?
Not recommended

How did they do with children (if present)?
No children present

How did they do with other dogs (if present)?
No other dogs present

If you select 'Not Recommended" to any of the answers above. Please use this space to tell us why you choice that selection.
He growled at a neighborhood cat, but was easy to call off of it! No animals in the home though.

How would you describe their energy level?
High

How were they on leash?
Pulled sometimes
Great!

Do you want to add any details about the information you provided above?

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
I would ABSOLUTELY adopt Ozzie. We immediately bonded and I adore him. He's so sweet and attuned and loving and I am so glad I got to meet him. If I could give him more time for the activity he needs I would totally keep him, but sadly my lifestyle wouldn't work for him. He has such a fun demeanor- INSANE heeler guy, but he knows how to turn it off. He's a blast, but a big family, a yard, and more consistent stimulation would be perfect for him. I'll miss him dearly whenever he gets adopted, and I've only had him for 3 days. <333

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
If you have another dog. Go on walks with Hambone and the other dog together for an introduction. He might need to be kept separate at first just to warm up. My dog has a lot of energy and bad communication skills so they got off to a bad start.

Now they are literally best friends and cuddle each other/play and do have any issues. He is mild to high energy so he probably needs another dog play with or a big backyard and 3 walks a day. He is still learning manors with people but is picking up quickly. After the 2nd time we tell him to stop something he listens!

Crate
Dog Bed

Relaxed

Some whining or pacing

Fully housetrained - Consistently holds it when left alone, and gives clear signals when they need to go outside. May have had accidents in the first couple days, but leveled out completely once the dog learned the routines.

Tolerant

Loved everyone

Not recommended

No children present

Warmed up over time

He has a high prey drive, really wants to hunt squirrels and gives similar stance and signals around cats in the neighborhood.

Moderate

Pulled sometimes

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
Yes absolutely. Only issue is his size, he’s a big boy! We are still deciding but he’s genuinely a perfect dog. Meet Eclipse: Your Future Furry Friend! 🌟

Eclipse is a delightful medium-sized poodle with a heart full of love and a tail that never stops wagging! This super friendly girl is always ready to greet everyone she meets with enthusiasm, making her the perfect companion for anyone looking for a little extra joy in their life.

Personality

• Energetic and Playful: Eclipse loves her daily adventures and thrives on plenty of walks. She’s eager to explore, sniff around, and meet new friends along the way.

• Cuddle Bug: After a good romp, this sweet girl is more than happy to curl up on the couch for some cozy snuggles.

Training and Manners

• House-Trained: Eclipse has mastered her potty training and is quick to do her business outside.

• Basic Commands: She already knows “sit” and “shake,” showcasing her intelligence and eagerness to learn.

• Room for Improvement: While she’s a fast learner, Eclipse will benefit from some additional training to curb her enthusiasm for placing her paws on counters and people.

Ideal Home

Eclipse would thrive in an active household where she can get the exercise she needs and plenty of love. Whether you’re an individual or a family, she’s ready to bring joy and companionship into your life.

If you’re looking for a smart, friendly, and playful pup to brighten your days, Eclipse is the one for you! Come meet her and see if you can resist those adorable tail wags!

animals.kennelCardMemo:
Mystic River: A Brave Heart in a Handsome Package

Don’t let his striking, athletic herding-dog looks fool you—Mystic River is a gentle soul who wears his heart on his sleeve. He is a master of the "slow and steady" approach to friendship, making every connection he builds incredibly special.

The Couragous Cuddler
Mystic River can be a little shy when first meeting new human friends. Instead of rushing in, he takes a moment to assess the room. But here is the most endearing thing about him: he is incredibly courageous. Even when he feels a bit timid, his desire for affection wins every time. You can watch his bravery in real-time as he slowly but surely inches his way over to lean against your legs for some well-deserved head scratches. Winning his trust is an incredibly rewarding experience that will make you feel like the most important person in the world.

Good Dog Friend
Mystic River he has successfully shared his space and been co-housed with another dog right here at the shelter. If you already have a dog looking for a buddy, Mystic River could be the match.

animals.name: Chocolate Caramel
animals.kennelCardMemo:
This puppy is going to be one of those dogs that makes you say, “Gosh, this is one of the best dogs I’ve ever had!” (And no shade to your past or current pups — we know they all hold a special place in your heart!)Sweet Chocolate Carmel just has a way of looking at you that says, “I love you a lot.” He’s a smart, fun boy who is ready for whatever adventure you have planned — even if that adventure is just a cozy day hanging out at home.

Chocolate Caramel's Impressive Skills: In less than two weeks, this buddy has already mastered "sit," is doing great with "wait" and "gentle," and understands "drop it" (even if giving up a prize is still a little tough!). He is crate trained, sleeping through the night like a champ with zero accidents or tears, and is already about 90% house-trained. Further training will be a breeze, not just because he’s incredibly smart, but because he has an enthusiasm for food that rivals the world's greatest chefs!

Dog & Cat Approved: Chocolate Caramel currently lives with a dog foster brother and loves to play. He would be thrilled to have a canine sibling in his adoptive home! Bonus points if they like to snuggle — while his foster brother loves to wrestle, he isn’t big on cuddling, and Chocolate Caramel is definitely looking for a cuddle buddy. He also lives with a cat who sets firm boundaries, and Chocolate Caramel is wonderfully respectful of her space.

Kid-Friendly: Chocolate Caramel absolutely loves kids! He is still learning that he can't play as roughly with humans as he does with other dogs, but he adores hanging out with the resident child, hosting her friends, and being part of the gang.

Anyone would be incredibly lucky to call this sweet puppy their own!

memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

animals.name: Poetry Unicorn
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Poetry Unicorn is a sweet, gentle 6-year-old German Shepherd who is looking for a loving person to call her own. Despite everything she’s been through, she has such a calm and affectionate personality and has quickly shown how much she loves being around her people.

Poetry Unicorn already knows several basic commands, including sit, come, and paw, and she is a very good listener at home. Her recall has been especially impressive, and she is eager to understand what you’re asking of her. She is still working on commands like stay, wait, and heel, particularly when there are lots of distractions, but she continues to improve with consistency and patience.

One of Poetry Unicorn’s sweetest qualities is how affectionate she is. She loves being petted and will even paw at you when she wants you to keep giving her attention. She enjoys being close to her person but also respects boundaries when asked. She has shown that she can settle comfortably in the home and is not destructive or overly demanding.

Poetry Unicorn is not reactive to people or other dogs. She may have a harder time focusing when there are lots of people, dogs, or other exciting things happening around her, but she does not show aggressive behavior and responds well to her handler. Her leash manners have already improved noticeably with regular walks.

She is also remarkably unfazed by loud household noises. Things like dishes clanking or loud sounds from the TV generally don’t bother her; sometimes she’ll briefly look toward the noise, but she doesn’t overreact.

Poetry Unicorn isn’t particularly food-motivated, especially outside, so she tends to respond better to praise, affection, and her relationship with her person than simply being bribed with treats.

Poetry Unicorn came to the shelter after her previous owner passed away and was later transferred to Austin Pets Alive following the Kerr County floods. She has been through a lot of change, but she has remained a loving, steady girl.

She would thrive with someone who is willing to continue building her confidence, manners, and obedience through positive, consistent training. She has already shown that she is smart, capable, affectionate, and eager to connect with her person.

If you’re looking for a loyal companion with a big heart, Poetry Unicorn may be your girl. ❤️y!

animals.name: Sansai
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Out of the challenges of the 2026 Texas floods emerged a remarkably bright and resilient spirit named Sansai. True to her name, which carries a sense of natural grace, she moves past her stormy beginnings with an unwavering, joyful outlook. Her regal posture combined with a fun-loving attitude makes her a striking and memorable presence the moment she catches your eye.

An eager adventurer, she greets the start of every walk with enthusiastic energy and a steady, manageable pace on her leash. While she maintains a calm kennel routine, her excitement builds naturally as she gets closer to the play yard. She shows a curious interest in toys like tennis balls, enjoys a stuffed toy, and loves nothing more than rolling around happily in the fresh green grass during her outdoor time.

Her companionable nature truly shines when it is time to connect closely with people. This sweet, happy girl is deeply affectionate, constantly seeking opportunities to lean in close for cuddles and gentle kisses. Her sociable disposition makes her a sweet, people-oriented companion who keeps her loving heart at the center of everything she does.

Your next great adventure and a lifetime of cozy couch cuddles are waiting just around the corner. Connect with us today to find out how you can bring this bright ray of sunshine into your life.

memos.Sleepover notes:
"How long was your Sleepover
It ends on 7/31 he has been out just 2 days.

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Chill
Curious
Treat/food motivated
Affectionate
Calm

What made you smile or laugh about them?
He sleeps on his belly with usually something like a "pillow" on his neck. He eats like "Kirby" so I recommend using a mat or slow feeder to pace himself while eating.

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
He was very nervous and scared of passing through all doors at the beginning, especially heavy/noisy doors. Be patient when introducing him to new areas. He's doing so much better now.
He was also scared about going to elevator but getting adjusted.
He's very scared of the shower, so if you're bathing him at home, use a cup or something to slowly drop water on him. He didn't like taking a bath but was amazingly calm when doing his nails (dremel).
He's doing great with a harness and leash. I'd recommend using a chest harness because he can pull sometimes. He gets really upset or mad if you pull on his collar, plus it's not safe for his neck.
Recommended a slow feeder or mat when giving him food and give his food separately, if you have other pets around.
Didn't care about apples nor the sandia. But he's very food-motivated.
He does great in his crate, he likes sometimes to rest or chill there; he slept in his crate the whole night without whining or any issues.
Loves being around others, either people or dogs, but also gives you space.

Where did the dog sleep
Crate
Dog Bed

How was the dog in the car?
Relaxed

How was the dog when left alone?
Relaxed
Some whining or pacing

What is their housetraining status?
Fully housetrained - Consistently holds it when left alone, and gives clear signals when they need to go outside. May have had accidents in the first couple days, but leveled out completely once the dog learned the routines.

How did the dog do in the bath?
Seemed nervous or anxious

How did they do with other adults in the home or visitors? Did they meet visitors, or only hang with you?
Loved everyone

How did they do with cats or small animals (if present)?
Not applicable

How did they do with children (if present)?
No children present

How did they do with other dogs (if present)?
Warmed up over time

How would you describe their energy level?
Moderate

How were they on leash?
Pulled sometimes

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
Definitely! Peppe is very chill for a puppy. It's a social butterfly. He's learning and gaining confidence very fast. Very sweet and playful boy, that also enjoys cuddling with you."

Lovely, Calm, Delightful


Don't be put off by her name. Stormy Beans is more like a gentle rainy afternoon than a Texas-sized thunderstorm. This chill girl is ready and eager for her forever family!

An utterly adorable tabby with the sweetest tiny meows, Stormy Beans was rescued from the recent flooding in Uvalde. After everything she's been through, she's learning that the world can be a safe and cozy place again. Stormy Beans is a shy girl at first, but every day she grows a little braver. She's started venturing beyond her favorite hiding spots to explore her foster home, and each day her confidence blooms.

She's not the type to leap into your lap or zoom around the house at top speed. Instead, Stormy Beans shows her affection in quieter ways. She likes being nearby while you go about your day. And, when you stop to pet her, she'll lean her whole little body into your hand and reward you with the most impressive full-body purrs. If you've been out for a while, don't be surprised if you're greeted by one of her delightfully precious meows saying, "Oh, you're back!"

Stormy Beans is a professional nap enthusiast and prefers relaxing over roughhousing. Treats, however, are another story. She'll happily wake up for snack time! She's curious, gentle, and easygoing, making her an excellent companion for someone who appreciates a peaceful household. She currently shares her foster home with another cat. While she's a little unsure around feline roommates and there have been a few harmless hisses, Stormy Beans is respectful and never looks to start trouble. She hasn't lived with dogs or children, though she's seen a dog without panicking. Because she's naturally cautious, she'd likely be happiest in a calm, quiet home without rambunctious kids, energetic puppies, or overly playful kittens.

Are you on the lookout for a gentle companion to add to your family? Contact us about Stormy Beans today!

Look out! Fresh on the scene is Max Headroom (Max), a rambunctious yet sweet little guy who adores spending time with those closest to him! When he’s in super excited kitty mode, he loves running around the house exploring all the nooks and crannies, tackling his sister and the couch, and jumping on any surface he can get his paws on! But, after a good play, when he calms down he will snuggle up with you on the couch or do biscuits on his favorite blankets while purring up a storm until he falls asleep!

Oftentimes, this little guy can be found zooming throughout the halls with his sister, as he absolutely ADORES kitty playtime! In particular, Max loves playing with mice on a string and will even put on an acrobatic show to get a hold of them! Thought he couldn’t get any cuter? This smart boy is on his way to learning how to fetch, and has already begun bringing his toys back to his foster parents for even more play sessions!

Max grew up with his sister, Columbo, and the two are deeply connected to one another. Oftentimes, these kitties can be found cuddling for comfort, eating together, or simply chasing each other’s tails throughout the halls, as they truly share a unique bond with one another. Ideally, Max would love to come home with his sister. Learn more about Columbo at the link below, and thank you for considering keeping these two lovebugs together! https://tinyurl.com/mr2ym3r2

Max sure is one special kitty: contact us today to arrange a meet & greet with him!

memos.Behavior Team FFU:
Sleepover host has not responded to placement team's attempts to contact her to get an update on Night Owl or to see if she would like to extend the sleepover or convert to foster/ adoption. I emailed the sleepover host and also texted her since I know she tends to respond better to text. AKC

*UPDATE 8/4/26: Sleepover host texted me back saying "She's a good girl. We will need some behavior work with her though. I don't know if we want to keep her or not. I'm gonna send you a video of her when we were walking down the street and she got really obnoxious. Mainly with dogs and at times humans. Anyway she's good with all of us. Connor [one of her adult sons who the last foster dog HEBuddy specifically didn't get along with] is at home. Garrett and Olivia [her other 2 adult children] are in Germany. Garrett's been in Germany for almost a month so he hasn't met the dog yet; however, I feel confident that there will be no problems with Garrett and the dog. We'll have to do the entry way with the treats like we with Buddy. She's not as good a walker on leash as Buddy. She's a very easy dog in the house. Although the word is still out on whether she's potty trained or not. She's been wearing a diaper since she got to my house. [Night Owl is noted to be in heat] I think she's getting it. You don't even know she's in the house." The sleepover host went on to say that she would like to get Night Owl around another dog because "I know she wants to play with someone, she wants to chew up some of them too I think". I think the sleepover host is referring to some on-leash reactivity (OLR) to dogs.

I replied offering a session to address basic obedience and manners training, including leash skills and OLR training. I asked if Night Owl has met anyone besides the people who live in the home. I explained that she may not require the same slow introduction routine that HEBuddy needed if she is not exhibiting the same fearful and defensive reactions that he did. I offered to schedule a PGA with her after she's recovered from her spay surgery. Lastly I asked the sleepover host to clarify what she meant by "keep her", so we know whether to extend the sleepover or convert to foster. AKC

What made you smile or laugh about them?
She smiles when she is happy. She is a big ol goofy lap dog. She loves to attack sprinklers

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
SHE IS AMAZING!!!!! Potty trained, not a single accident in the house in six days. She is kennel trained and sleeps in there all night without concern. She knows basic commands like sit and shake and sometimes lay down.

The only time she tries to go out the front door is if I am going out but stops and stays when I tell her to. She has not barked in the house but will bark at people talking on the other side of the fence, although it is not often. She seems fascinated by squirrels.

She does not have separation anxiety or bark when the garage door opens. She is not motivated by food or treats but will take one when I give my dog one. She does not want to eat just kibble so I mix in a tiny bit of gravy and she scarfs it down. She doesn't really beg for food when I am eating and if she gets too close I tell her no and she goes and lays down. I have been calling her Piper and she is starting to respond to it.

She is very easily redirected and listens to no and stop. Her one bad habit, which mostly is because I am not used to it, is that she paws at you when she wants to be pet. As soon as you pet her, she stops, but as soon as you stop, she starts pawing again. It is very gentle and I am trying to break her of this habit.

While she does follow me everywhere I go, she does not necessarily need attention, she just wants to be in the same room. If I am on the couch, she waits for permission but does get on it on her own when no one else is on it. My favorite silly thing about her is that she LOVES sprinklers and will beeline right to it and put her whole mouth on the small ones and chomps at the water from the bigger one. She walks well on a leash, unless she sees a sprinkler and then pulls (not too hard) to get to it.

animals.name: Cactus Guy
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Do not let the name fool you, because this cheerful fellow is absolutely nothing like a prickly desert plant. He is a stunning dog with a smooth, warm fawn coat, highly expressive rose ears that frame his face, and a massive, joyful smile that instantly highlights his sweet nature. Arriving as a brave survivor during the 2026 Texas floods, he has consistently proven that he is all warmth and zero thorns.

He is an extremely friendly, high-energy companion who is always eager to participate in shelter playgroups with other dogs. His sociable and playful spirit makes him an approachable presence in social settings, where he genuinely enjoys interacting with his canine peers. When he is not showing off his vibrant energy, he turns on the charm with a pair of masterful puppy-dog eyes that he uses to score extra attention.

During outings, his affectionate side takes center stage as he actively looks for a bunch of pets, loving, and cozy cuddles. He matches his athletic, playful drive with a deep desire for close companionship and human connection. Come down and meet Cactus Guy to bring a lifetime of sunny devotion into your home today.

animals.kennelCardMemo:
Stepping into the spotlight with a bright, open smile and an unmistakable zest for life, Grady is a handsome fellow who knows how to make a memorable first impression. His striking, beautifully symmetric markings complement a genuinely happy face that radiates positivity. He approaches the world with a vibrant, puppy-like energy that instantly lifts the mood of anyone nearby.

This active gentleman is a huge enthusiast for his daily walks, treating every outdoor excursion as an exciting adventure. While he certainly has a healthy appreciation for snacks, his companionable nature means he likes people even more than treats. He is always ready to pivot his attention toward human friends, showing a sweet, approachable disposition that makes building a bond effortless.

His social background includes navigating the historic 2026 Texas floods, and he has since become a regular participant in shelter dog playgroups. Notes show he is good with dogs, balancing his canine interactions with a strong focus on human connection. Grady keeps his people-oriented affection at the center of everything he does, making him a wonderful partner for outdoor time.

An energetic, affectionate partner is ready to turn ordinary days into extraordinary adventures. Skip the wait and schedule a time to experience Grady's contagious joy firsthand, whether you want to open your home for fostering or find a lifetime teammate.

memos.Disclaimer: Animal intaked during 2026 Central Texas flood

The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

If you are looking for a sweet, gentle, and utterly devoted companion to bring pure sunshine into your life, Bailey Denise Puff is ready to smile her way into your heart!

She carries her history with a gentle grace, approaching the world with a steady curiosity that instantly warms the room.

Her sunny disposition shines through brightest when it is time to explore the outdoors. She treats every path as an open book, thoroughly enjoying long walks where she can take her time sniffing the grass and catching the scents on the breeze. This companionable nature extends easily to social settings, where she shows a good-natured approach to daily activities.

Building connections comes naturally to her, whether she is mingling in structured shelter dog play groups or interacting gently with children. She maintains an approachable, sociable energy that bridges the gap between playtime and quiet companionship. Her balanced attitude makes her a comforting presence, showing a sweet disposition to everyone she meets along the way.

Finding a loyal friend to share life's simple adventures has never been easier.

memos.Foster Notes:
Shadow truly stands out because of his confident, social, intelligent, and go-with-the-flow personality. He gets along with everyone and every dog we have encountered, making him the perfect companion to take anywhere—whether it's a farmers market, outdoor dining, hiking, or swimming.

To help him transition smoothly, here are a few notes on his care and routine:

- Exercise & Socialization: Shadow needs both mental and physical exercise. He loves and needs to play with other dogs. He has thrived in our home with our two dogs (one low energy and one high energy) and does well with both.
- Habits & Training: He definitely has some retriever in him, as he loves to pick things up in his mouth and carry them around, which is super cute. However, he will chew on things he shouldn't. We suggest keeping items like shoes, clothes, socks, glasses, and remotes out of his reach. He is a good listener, intelligent, and eager to learn, so at this stage, it is just about redirecting his attention.
- Leash Walking: He is new to the leash, so we suggest using a harness with a front clip to help with pulling.
- Sleeping Routine: At night, we keep him in a gated area in our bedroom with his bed, a blanket, and durable chew toys. As long as he can see us, he sleeps through the night.
- Potty Training: He is about 95% potty trained. Because we work from home and have a fenced yard, we have been letting him out every two hours

Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions at all.

animals.kennelCardMemo:

She is initially shy in new situations, preferring to take a moment to quietly observe her surroundings from a safe vantage point. She loves to explore her environment, tracking interesting scents and sniffing every single object with quiet, focused dedication. This gentle soul gets along well with other dogs and is looking for a peaceful home where she can share her sweet wisdom and steady devotion. Welcome The Hierophant into your life today to discover the deep loyalty of a truly special companion.

memos.Behavioral: 8/6 - Not in a good spot, reactive on exit IC
memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.
